newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up in active trading on Wednesday, thanks to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The key December 1996 contract ended at 21,180 yuan ($2,549) per tonne, rising 120 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 21,400 and hit a low of 20,960.
September fell 20 to 21,380 yuan. October rose 40 to 21,290, November 30 to 21,150, the January 1997 contract 100 to 21,180, February 110 to 21,200, March 160 to 21,200 and April 390 to 21,200.
Combined volume fell to 57,710 tonnes from 77,940.
"Copper will not breach the range of 21,000 and 21,500 yuan in the short term, until LME gives a clear direction," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended down. September fell 40 to 14,370 yuan. October did not trade. November dropped 40 to 14,350.
Combined volume rose to 410 tonnes from 120.
